# Capability Matrix

OS APIs and system capabilities per component: raw disk access, VSS, WMI, crypto, networking, IPC.
**Source of truth:** `inventory/pe-analysis.json` (535 PEs, full import/export DB, generated by
`scripts/pe_deep_analysis.py`). Findings below cite that data — verify any claim against it.

**Status:** substantially complete for core modules (session 2). Satellite tools pending detail pass.

---

## 1. Scan engine contract (all nine engines)

Every filesystem engine DLL (NTFS/FAT/exFAT/EXT4/Btrfs/HFS+/ReFS/ZFS) exports exactly two
factory functions, both 64-bit:

| DLL | Exports |
|---|---|
| NTFSSearchDLL.dll | `EUCreateNTFSQuickSearcher`, `EUCreateNTFSSearcher` |
| FATSearchDLL.dll | `EUCreateFATQuickSearcher`, `EUCreateFATSearcher` |
| exFATSearchDLL.dll | `EUCreateEXFATQuickSearcher`, `EUCreateEXFATSearcher` |
| EXT4SearchDLL.dll | `EUCreateEXT4QuickSearcher`, `EUCreateEXT4Searcher` |
| BtrfsSearchDLL.dll | `EUCreateBtrfsQuickSearcher`, `EUCreateBtrfsComplateSearcher` (sic) |
| HFSPlusSearchDLL.dll | `EUCreateHFSQuickSearcher`, `EUCreateHFSSearcher` |
| ReFSSearchDLL.dll | `EUCreateReFSQuickSearcher`, `EUCreateReFSSearcher` |
| ZfsSearchDLL.dll | `EUCreateZFSQuickSearcher`, `EUCreateZFSSearcher` |
| RAWSearchDLL.dll | `EUCreateRAWSearcher`, `EUCreateRAWSearcherForCellTest`, `EUGetAnalyserList`, `EUGetAnalyserMap`, `EUGetAnalyserMultimap`, `GetRawUserInfoMap` |

**Design reading (for Recovarr):** a uniform engine interface where Quick = metadata-driven scan
(MFT/FAT/inode walk) and Full = deep structure+carve scan. RAWSearchDLL is the signature-carving
engine with a self-describing analyser registry — the host can enumerate available carvers at runtime.
Our Rust equivalent: a `Searcher` trait with `quick()`/`deep()` constructors per filesystem crate,
plus a `CarverRegistry` that is queryable.

### Disk I/O pattern (imports)

- Engines open volumes via `CreateFileW` (volume handles), read via **memory mapping**
  (`CreateFileMappingW` + `MapViewOfFile`) and/or `DeviceIoControl`, with `CreateEventW` for
  async completion signaling. exFAT/FAT also use `CreateFileA`/`WriteFile` (log/progress writes).
- HFS+/ReFS engines import no CreateFile family at all — they receive a mapped view or handle
  from the host (stronger evidence that the host owns device opening and passes context).
- NTFSSearchDLL: 13 import DLLs / 99 functions — the richest engine (USN/journal work).

## 2. Host application — DRWUI.exe (amd64, GUI, ASLR+NX)

- Qt5 Widgets monolith: imports qt5widgets (1,246 fns), qt5core (871), qt5gui (337), msvcp140 (278),
  kernel32 (218). **3,610 imported functions across 49 DLLs.** No Qt Quick in the main UI
  (Qt Quick only inside the embedded diskhealth sub-product).
- Exports a tiny COM-like component system: `IObject` with `AddRef`, `GetInterfaceEx`, move/assign
  ctors — an in-process plugin/interface bus.
- Elevation: `CreateProcessAsUserW`, `CreateProcessWithTokenW`, `CreateProcessW/A`, `ShellExecuteExW`,
  `AdjustTokenPrivileges` — spawns elevated helpers rather than running elevated itself.
- Raw disk: `DeviceIoControl` in imports — direct IOCTL path in addition to engines.
- Networking: `HttpOpenRequestW`, `InternetOpenW` (WinInet) — licensing/telemetry/update checks.
- Crypto: `CryptAcquireContext*`, `CryptHashData`, `BCryptGenRandom` — license validation +
  random seeding.

## 3. Elevation & kernel layer

| Component | Role | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| DRWService.exe | **BitlockerReadFVEService** — self-installing Windows service that reads BitLocker FVE metadata/keys and serves decrypted volume reads over named pipe `\\.\Pipe\DRWBitlocker` | strings + CreateServiceA/RegisterServiceCtrlHandlerA + SetNamedPipeHandleState + WaitNamedPipeA; PDB path `BitlockerReadFVEService.pdb` |
| eprdtdrv.sys (PartitionRecovery) | minimal raw-disk filter driver, ntoskrnl-only imports (41 fns, IoBuildDeviceIoControlRequest/IofCallDriver) — direct sector access bypassing filesystem stack | PE imports |
| EuMrx.sys (EuShare) | full SMB **mini-redirector driver** (183 ntoskrnl imports + ksecdd) — kernel-mode NAS access for the NAS recovery feature | PE imports |
| setupdrvx64.exe (PartitionRecovery) | driver installer helper (EPM shared component; PDB `setupempdrvx64.pdb`, project `mod.WinDiskAccessDriverSetup`) | strings |
| WinPE drivers (regdrv.reg) | `epmdkdrv.sys`, `EUDCPEPM.sys`, `EUEDKEPM.sys` registered into the PE system hive — the bootable environment's raw-access/disk-copy driver set | BUILDPE/x64/regdrv.reg |

## 4. WinPE bootable subsystem (BUILDPE/, 177 MB)

- `EaseUS-x64/` — the full recovery product (same engines + UI) for the PE environment.
- `x64/` — WinPE shell platform: `auto.bat` boot script builds a desktop (winxshell explorer,
  PENetwork, Chrome as image/pdf viewer via `--app=` kiosk registration, diskmgmt/devmgmt MMC
  shortcuts, Boot Repair + DiskHealth/DiskMark conditionally copied from the boot USB).
- Platform is **shared across EaseUS products** (references `SOFTWARE\EASEUS\EPM\Version` —
  Partition Master lineage; mainland-China builds behave differently via OEM flag).
- `Dict/` — dictionary/wordlist assets (password/repair related — detail pass pending).
- `DRWReport.ini` — log file inventory: `DelFat.log` (FAT high-cluster recovery), `DRWUI.log`,
  `DefaultLog.txt`, `Drwdump0-5.DMP` (ring of crash dumps), `BuildRaw.log` (raw file counts).

## 5. Bitness strategy

- **Core scan path is pure amd64**: DRWUI + all engines + drivers + service.
- 32-bit satellites: file-repair suite (ImageMagick CORE_RL_* + libheif + libde265 + libcurl 8 +
  OpenSSL 3), VideoViewer (FFmpeg 6 + ZeroMQ 4.3.5), diskhealth (own full Qt Quick runtime, own
  .rcc), EUinApp.exe (VS2008-era msvcr90 — ancient in-app purchase code), EuDownloader,
  unins000 (Inno Setup), 7za.exe.
- Root also ships OpenSSL 1.1 (`libcrypto-1_1`, `libssl-1_1`) + legacy `libeay32MD/ssleay32MD`
  (OpenSSL 1.0 era) — three crypto generations coexist.

## 6. Carving engine internals (RAWSearchDLL)

RTTI names leak the complete carver class hierarchy (structure knowledge, not copied code):

- Interface layer: `IRawFileAnalyser`, `AEPAnalyser` (AfterEffects), `IObject` base.
- Carver families organized by authoring namespace:
  - `CFile*Analyser` — simple header carvers: JPG, PNG, ZIP, PDF, OLE (doc/xls/ppt container),
    PST, PSD, MKV, EMF, WMF, RAR, TAR, TTF, SWF, SVG, RTF, HTM, ICO, BMP, GZ, LZH, SIT, CAB,
    CHM, HLP, MID, MDB, MNY, MPG, MRW, ONE, PSP, RM/RMVB, WPD, X3F, 3GP, AU, FLV, DMG, CPT,
    FCPEVENT, LowDoc.
  - `*Analyser@BruteForce` — structural brute-force carvers: Jpeg, MP3, Mov, Pdf, Tiff, M2TS,
    MTS, ASF, APE, ADTS, DWG, DXF, EPS, GPX, GIF, FCPEvt, CFH11.
  - `*Analyser@RawSpeed` — speed-optimized: PNG, RAR, TAR, RTF, HTML, MID, OGG, GZ, SIT, PSP,
    ONE, DBX (Outlook Express), 3DS, WPG, MDB.
  - `*Analyser@Brance` / `RawFormat_xjq` — vendor-family additions: FLV, DMG, LZH, MPG, MXF,
    RIFF, RM, SVG, X3F, CRW (Canon RAW), HEIC, JP2, M1V, MOBI, CommonRaw (generic RAW fallback).
- Each carver has a paired `*RawFileInfo` value class (parsed metadata).
- MP4 handling: brand strings `ftypmp41/2`, `ftypmmp4`, `XAVCmp4` + `GetIMovMp4Repair` export —
  video repair is integrated into the carving path for recoverable-but-damaged MP4/MOV.
- Two-tier design: dedicated C++ carvers for common formats; `raw_signs.json` generic signature
  table for the long tail (139 formats, 261 patterns — schema in §7).

## 7. raw_signs.json schema (documented for our own DB design — values NOT copied)

```
"<format-id>": {
  "header": { "signs": ["<decimal-offset>,<hex-bytes>,<confidence 0-1>", ...] },
  "tail":   { "signs": [...] },          // optional footer signature
  "min": <min plausible size>,           // size-gating before accepting
  "max": <max plausible size>
}
```

- Multiple signs per format vote with per-sign confidence weights; min/max sizes act as a
  plausibility gate (anti-false-positive). 46/139 formats also verify the tail.
- Notably absent from the table: jpg/png/zip/mp4/rar — exactly the formats with dedicated C++
  carvers, confirming the two-tier split.
- **Recovarr rule:** our signature DB will be written from published format specifications
  (file signature literature, format docs), not by transcribing this file.

## 8. Monetization / licensing architecture (what the free build gates)

Strings evidence (DRWUI):

- Free: "recovers up to %1 data" (2 GB); Trial: "preview-only". Pro: unlimited.
- Per-feature upsell funnels: `*_Click_Upgrade_Linux`, `_Nas`, `_SD`, `_Doc`, `_Video` —
  Linux recovery, NAS recovery, SD-card deep features, document repair, video repair are
  separately gated SKUs.
- License format `XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX`; activation server `activation.easeus.site`;
  states: invalid/used/locked/expired/pirate; auto-activation after payment (2Checkout
  `parse2COPlatfromLicense`, in-app purchase via EUinApp.exe, mainland flow
  `doActivateMainlandProduct`); trial state persisted in registry
  `SOFTWARE\DRWNewTrial\Metadata` + `recoveryTrial.ini`.
- ENS (embedded notification service?) ad placements with screen coordinates in config.ini.

**Recovarr implication:** every one of these gates becomes a free feature for us; the list is
the definition of "feature parity target".

## 9. IPC map

| Channel | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `\\.\Pipe\DRWBitlocker` | DRWUI ↔ DRWService (BitLocker volume reads) |
| ZeroMQ (VideoViewer ships libzmq-mt-4_3_5.dll) | video preview/repair process control |
| DRWLoader / launcher | DRW.exe → DRWUI.exe handoff (bootstrapper chain, 634 strings, detail pass pending) |
| WinInet HTTPS | licensing, telemetry (Firebase remote config via firebasefetch.exe; crash upload via send_dmp_with_aliyun.exe / AliyunWrap) |
| Firebase remote config | feature flags fetched at runtime (firebasefetch.exe) |

## 10. Cross-component security posture (for our threat model)

- Drivers unsigned-adjacent legacy (eprdtdrv.sys no ASLR/NX flags in PE — normal for .sys but
  noteworthy), service self-installs on demand (CreateServiceA at runtime = persistence surface
  we will replace with an MSI/service installer + least-privilege design).
- WinPE auto.bat registers Chrome as the file viewer — kiosk `--app=` mode.
- Three OpenSSL generations in-tree (1.0/1.1/3.x) — dependency hygiene lesson for us: single
  rustls/ring stack, no C crypto zoo.
